extracted.intended_audience: researchers, clinicians, and instrument developers performing/assessing measurement validation and reliability studies (psychometrics/clinical assessment)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical standards for assessing validity, inter-rater/intra-rater/test-retest reliability, and implementation/feasibility of clinical measurement instruments, classification systems, and point-of-care tests across healthcare and rehabilitation settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability (kappa statistic and percent agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Item-level agreement between data collectors was assessed with both the kappa statistic and percent agreement (e.g., reported kappa ranges, and item-level kappas used to judge reliability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohen's kappa (or weighted kappa where appropriate) and percent agreement to quantify inter-rater agreement for discrete items. Report kappa with interpretation (examples in text: κ=0.37–0.96 observed; κ=0.80–0.96 described as 'almost perfect'; κ=0.61–0.79 as 'substantial').

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability for summary scores (intraclass correlation coefficient)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-rater reliability of school summary scores and other composite measures was measured using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate ICC model (report model and confidence intervals) to assess reliability of continuous or aggregated scores across raters; report ICC values and 95% CIs (examples: ICC=0.90–1.00, ICC=0.81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-retest reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability over time (test-retest) was assessed by repeating measurements and calculating ICCs or kappa for stability across sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain repeat assessments separated by an appropriate interval and compute ICC or kappa for test-retest reliability; report ranges and confidence intervals. Example: videotaped tests performed twice and scored to determine test-retest ICC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Intra-rater reliability was assessed by having the same rater score items or videos on separate occasions and computing kappa or ICC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include repeated ratings by the same rater to estimate consistency; report weighted kappa or ICC with confidence intervals (examples: weighted kappa k_w = 0.66–1.00 for intra-rater).

rubrics_metrics.name: Face validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Face validity was assessed via expert or stakeholder surveys indicating whether the scoring scheme appears appropriate (e.g., 92% of nurses agreed with RASS scoring scheme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect surveys of subject matter experts or end-users to document perceived appropriateness of items/scoring; report proportions agreeing/strongly agreeing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content validity (expert importance ratings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content validity was evaluated by subject matter experts rating the clinical importance of items (e.g., nephrologists rated 18 adverse effects 3.1 ± 0.75 out of 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use panels of experts to rate item relevance/importance and report mean ratings and variability to support content validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct validity (known-groups and convergent measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct validity was demonstrated by the instrument distinguishing between known groups or correlating with related constructs (e.g., higher GI adverse effects in one drug group; RASS correlated with attention tests, GCS, medication doses, EEG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test hypotheses about expected differences or correlations (use statistical tests like t-tests, regression, correlation coefficients) and report p-values/effect sizes to support construct validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion validity (correlation with reference standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion validity was assessed by correlating instrument scores with reference standard ratings or established measures (e.g., RASS validity correlated with reference standard ratings and GCS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare instrument scores against accepted reference standards and report correlation coefficients and significance to demonstrate criterion validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity and specificity (diagnostic/point-of-care tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic performance for point-of-care tests was evaluated using sensitivity and specificity against a composite reference standard (examples: IsoScreen sensitivity 93.2%, specificity 98.7%; SmokeScreen sensitivity 69.2%, specificity 81.6%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sensitivity, specificity, and confidence intervals; explore covariates related to false positives/negatives via regression analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal consistency of items for latent constructs (e.g., Communicator and Collaborator competencies) was assessed using Cronbach's alpha (e.g., α = 0.997).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute Cronbach's alpha for item sets measuring the same construct and report 95% CIs; note that extremely high alpha may indicate redundancy and poor discriminatory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory power (ability to differentiate participants)
rubrics_metrics.description: An instrument's capacity to discriminate among trainee performance or clinical states was evaluated (Team StACER lacked discriminatory power as all trainees scored 'meets requirements').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess score distribution and ceiling/floor effects; determine whether the instrument differentiates levels of performance; consider revising items or scoring if discriminatory power is poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and acceptability (time, training, user satisfaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility and acceptability were measured by recording time for rater training, test administration and scoring, and user satisfaction surveys (e.g., MA2 feasible/acceptable; PharmDISC user satisfaction median ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect metrics on training time, administration and scoring burden, and user feedback; report median/means and qualitative suggestions for implementation (e.g., need for electronic tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement error indices such as standard error of measurement and minimal detectable change were determined for morphology, joint excursion, strength, and motor control measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate SEM and MDC to quantify absolute measurement error and to inform clinical interpretation of score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and back-translation procedures for cross-language instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation of instruments included forward translation and approval of back translation by the original authors (e.g., German translation of MA2 approved by original authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bilingual translators, perform back-translation, and obtain confirmation from original instrument authors; document translation process to support content equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration and norming workshops for rubric scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitated calibration workshops and guided discussion were used to norm rubric criteria among raters (e.g., VALUE rubric calibration to improve inter-rater consistency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use iterative workshops with sample work to align raters' interpretations; follow with independent scoring exercises to quantify inter-rater reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of model items/examples and training materials to improve agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability studies used model PIs, certification, and supporting materials (e.g., ISAT training, PharmDISC model PIs) to standardize data collectors/raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide model examples, certification, and structured training; evaluate agreement after training and use model cases to benchmark rater performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness/appropriateness/interpretability of classification
rubrics_metrics.description: For classification systems, appropriateness, interpretability, and the ratio of completely classified items were tracked (e.g., 82.9% of PIs were completely classified in PharmDISC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure proportion of items fully classifiable, rate interpretability and appropriateness via user assessment, and identify barriers (time, understanding benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Fleiss's kappa for multi-rater categorical classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrater reliability for classification systems with multiple raters was measured using Fleiss's kappa (PharmDISC average κ = 0.66).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Fleiss's kappa when more than two raters classify nominal categories; report kappa and interpret per standard benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of confidence intervals for reliability estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability and validity statistics were reported with confidence intervals (e.g., ICC 95%-confidence intervals 0.78-1.00; intra-class correlation 0.81 (95% CI: 0.65-0.90)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always report 95% CIs for ICCs, kappa, sensitivity/specificity, and other estimates to convey precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate statistical tests for feature-diagnosis associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Features' diagnostic utility was tested with Fisher's exact test and other inferential methods to compare proportions between cases and controls (example: MRI features compared with true diagnosis using Fisher's two-sided exact test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate hypothesis tests (Fisher's exact, chi-square, t-tests, regression) depending on data structure to evaluate whether features discriminate diagnostic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of context and information effects on observer variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Observer agreement may depend on additional information and timing (example: surgeons' classification agreement changed when patient history or radiographs were provided; CT diagnostic agreement worsened with delayed scanning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reliability studies to examine effects of contextual information, blinding/unblinding, and timing; report how additional data influence inter- and intra-rater agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple convergent validity checks (multi-method construct testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct validity can be strengthened by using several methods (e.g., correlation with attention screening, GCS, medication dosages, EEG, clinical outcomes such as extubation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine different measures and statistical approaches to triangulate construct validity; report correlation coefficients and significance for each convergent measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and sampling procedures for reliability audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability audits were specified (e.g., simultaneous audits by two independent, certified data collectors for a minimum of two schools or at least 5% of the school sample; audits conducted at 20.7% of schools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and report audit/sample size rules used to estimate reliability (minimum numbers or percentage of sample); use paired independent assessments to compute agreement statistics.
